Tune Design-MFA Components with Held-Out Subjects

Source: R/design_mfa_tune.R
tune_design_mfa.Rd

Selects component rank, spatial smoothness, fixed partial-pooling penalties, and soft-alignment stabilization using subject-disjoint folds. For each fold, a candidate effect is learned from analysis subjects and compared with the same design-effect matrix estimated independently from assessment subjects.

Usage

tune_design_mfa(
  Y,
  design,
  formula,
  subject = NULL,
  terms = NULL,
  grid = NULL,
  n_folds = 3L,
  seed = 1L,
  refit = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

Y

A named list of subject trial-by-feature matrices.

design

A matching list of trial-design data frames.

formula

A one-sided design formula passed to [design_mfa()].

subject

Optional unique subject identifiers.

terms

Optional terms scored during tuning. The default scores every requested formula term.

grid

Candidate data frame or named list with `rank`, `spatial_penalty`, `subject_penalty`, and `alignment_penalty` fields.

n_folds

Number of subject-disjoint folds. Every assessment fold must contain at least two subjects.

seed

Seed for deterministic named-subject fold construction. The caller's global random-number state is restored on successful and error exits.

refit

Refit [design_mfa()] on all subjects with the selected values.

verbose

Report failed candidate-fold fits as they occur.

...

Fixed arguments passed to [design_mfa()]. Tuned fields and `store` are controlled by this function.

Value

A `design_mfa_tuning` object containing candidate summaries, fold-level scores, retained failure diagnostics, subject membership, selected parameters, and the full refit when `refit = TRUE`.

Details

The score is the mean, over estimable requested terms, of reference-weighted squared disagreement divided by the held-out effect energy. This measures recovery of a separately estimated design effect, not trial-response prediction. Each analysis fold derives its reference grid/weights without assessment responses, and that same target grid/weights is used for its assessment fit. Spatial generalized components are reconstructed with their dual metric loadings. Every candidate must succeed on every fold to be eligible. Failed candidate-fold fits remain visible in `fold_scores` and are aggregated in `failure_summary`; an otherwise successful tuning run warns when any candidate was excluded by a fit failure.

This procedure selects hyperparameters; its minimum score is not an unbiased estimate of final performance. For outer-subject performance assessment, run `tune_design_mfa()` inside an outer subject-level resampling loop.

Examples

# \donttest{
example_data <- design_mfa_example_data()
tuned <- tune_design_mfa(
  example_data$Y, example_data$design, ~ saliency,
  terms = "saliency", grid = data.frame(rank = c(1L, 2L)),
  n_folds = 3, seed = 11, refit = FALSE
)
tuned$best_params
#> $rank
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $spatial_penalty
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $subject_penalty
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $alignment_penalty
#> [1] 0
#> 
# }
